To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effective aperture of a CRL is determined not by its real aperture, but by its absorption.
the real aperture of a CRL has no influence on the focusing properties of the lens, and that the effective aperture of a Crl is determined by absorption.

for a strongly attenuating CRL the real size of the CRL does not affect its focusing properties and that for a weakly attenuating CRL, the effective aperture of a CRL is defined by the integral intensity of a beam behind the lens over its real aperture.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of the effective aperture for the X-ray CRL.
the effective aperture of X-ray lenses, the aperture function of the two-dimensional Crl and a new approximation for the two-dimensional CRI.
the effective aperture of CRLs, which determines the focusing properties of the X-ray lenses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effective aperture of a CRL is determined by absorption and that the Kohn definition is the most correct.

the effective aperture of a linear CRL is the real aperture, while the effective aperture of circular and two-dimensional CRLs is the effective aperture of an equivalent linear CRL with the same absorption.
the effective aperture of CRLs is determined by absorption and is independent of real aperture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effective aperture is the aperture that is determined by absorption only and is independent of the real aperture.
the effective aperture of a CRL is the area where the intensity of the beam is greater than 1/e of the maximum intensity value.

for a strongly absorptive CRL the effective aperture is equal to the real aperture and for weakly absorbing CRL the effective apertures are 6% and 41% greater than the real apertures, according to the Kohn and Lengeler definitions, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effective aperture of a CRL is determined only by the absorption of the material, and the real aperture does influence the effective aperture only for transparent CRLs.
for a strongly focusing CRL, one should use the effective aperture instead of the real aperture.
it is necessary to use the new definition of the aperture for transparent CRLs in order to compare different CRL designs and to optimize their parameters.
